subject: Human Evolution
title: The Megafauna Extinctions
description: A quick, practical guide to The Megafauna Extinctions.

hook.text: Mammoths, giant sloths, cave bears, saber-toothed cats—all gone within a few thousand years. Coincidence?

buildup.text: The extinctions happened on every continent shortly after humans arrived—Australia, Americas, Europe.

discovery.text: The 'overkill hypothesis' blames human hunting for wiping out animals that had never seen such predators.

twist.text: Climate change at the end of the ice age also shrank habitats. Most likely, both factors combined.

climax.text: Megafauna that evolved alongside African humans survived. Those meeting humans for the first time did not.

punchline.text: Unfamiliar with us, they never learned to run.

quiz.question: Why did megafauna outside Africa go extinct?
options: Likely a combination of human hunting and climate change
